item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Yubing Qian, Weiluo Ren, Ji Chen
arXiv:2610.28095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural network fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states offer a promising alternative for capturing Landau level (LL) mixing and for understanding FQH physics, yet the incorporation of physical priors has so far been limited to the minimal exact constraints built into the ansatz. In the former case, the monopole harmonic product orbital (MHPO) ansatz is difficult to optimize, whereas in the latter, the expressivity of the neural network is restricted. item.title: Graph-Theoretic Analysis of Phase Optimization Complexity in Variational Wave Functions for Heisenberg Antiferromagnets
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Mahmud Ashraf Shamim, Md Moshiur Rahman Raj, Mohamed Hibat-Allah, Paulo T Araujo
arXiv:2602.04943v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the computational complexity of learning the ground state phase structure of Heisenberg antiferromagnets. Representing Hilbert space as a weighted graph, the variational energy defines a weighted XY model that, for Z₂ phases, reduces to a classical antiferromagnetic Ising model on that graph. For fixed amplitudes, reconstructing the signs of the ground state wavefunction thus reduces to a weighted Max-Cut instance. This links sign optimization of wavefunctions directly to combinatorial optimization.

item.title: Quantum Kolmogorov--Arnold networks are classically reproducible at their attained accuracy, and a discrete-logarithm encoding need not be: a measurement-based map of where quantum advantage can live
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Hikaru Wakaura
Quantum machine-learning models are useful only if classical computers cannot cheaply imitate them. We test this directly for quantum Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (QKANs)---neural networks whose tunable ``activation functions'' are small quantum circuits---by asking whether each model can be contracted as an efficient tensor network (TN). Our task-aware yardstick is the bond dimension a classical surrogate needs to copy the model's output at the accuracy the model itself reaches. We find a clear ladder. The amplitude-encoded Chebyshev QKAN uses only logarithmically many qubits and is exactly classical. arXiv:2610.28023v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conventional Fermi-liquid theories of dense nuclear matter predict that the direct Urca process requires a proton fraction above a threshold of Yₚ approx 0.11--0.15, which is rarely reached in low-mass neutron stars. In the non-Fermi-liquid regimes, nucleons have a smooth momentum occupation without a sharp Fermi surface, and their chemical potentials develop a logarithmic temperature dependence. item.title: Giant Spin-to-Charge Conversion by Tailoring Magnetically Proximitized Topological Dirac Semimetal
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Masayuki Ishida, Soichiro Fukuoka, Takahiro Chiba, Yohei Kota, Masaaki Tanaka, Le Duc Anh
arXiv:2507.17639v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The role of magnetic proximity on topological surface states (TSSs) and spin-to-charge conversion efficiency is studied in Fe/topological Dirac semimetal α-Sn heterostructures. As α-Sn thickness increases (9-38 nm), the damping constant of Fe peaks at 25 nm and then decreases. Theoretical modeling links this to long-range magnetic proximity effects (MPE) that suppress TSSs at the Fe/α-Sn interface while opening an exchange gap at the opposite interface. At 25 nm, we achieve an inverse Edelstein length of -3.1±1.0 nm, one of the highest values at room temperature, highlighting MPE's importance in spintronics.

To enable rapid integrity assessment of buried natural gas pipelines subjected to construction surcharge loading, a three-dimensional ABAQUS finite element model incorporating nonlinear pipe–soil contact was developed. The model was validated through mesh-independence analysis and comparison with experimental data reported in the literature, yielding a mean error of 6.32%. item.title: Anchored Exploration in Product Evolution: A Phylogenetic Network Framework for Semiconductor Designs
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Huy Nguyen, Dawoon Jeong
arXiv:2610.26973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a product phylogenetic network framework for examining anchored exploration. Using 102,465 semiconductor products grouped into 45,996 design families, we distinguish accumulated design continuity (Anchor) from externally precedented feature additions (horizontal transfer, HT). Fitted regressions yield non-monotonic relationships for HT occurrence and descendant carriage, alongside increasing within-family carriage over observed support. These patterns connect technological trajectories and recombination by distinguishing the continuity associated with incorporating external features from that associated with reproducing them in subsequent products.
